paper.title_en: Prethermalization of entanglement entropy in the mixed-field Ising model
paper.abstract_en: We study how weak integrability breaking affects the dynamics of the half-chain entanglement entropy of random product states in the mixed-field Ising model. The associated Hamiltonian depends on two parameters $g$ and $h$ determining the sizes of the longitudinal and transverse fields and has two integrable limits: the classical Ising chain $(h=0)$ and the transverse-field Ising model $(g=0)$. Weak perturbations of these limits give rise to the short-range network (SRN) and long-range network (LRN) regimes, respectively. We characterize the departure from integrable dynamics and the emergence of intermediate entanglement plateaus by melting times $T_M$ at prescribed entropy thresholds and analyze their dependence on the perturbation strength. For the SRN parameters examined away from $g=2$, we find $T_M\propto h^{-2}$ over the thresholds tested. At $g=2$, the relaxation splits into two stages: an initial departure from the integrable plateau with $T_M\propto h^{-1}$, followed by the melting of a well-defined intermediate prethermal plateau with $T_{M_2}\propto h^{-2}$. In the LRN regime, by contrast, the inverse of $T_M$ scales with exponents of $g$ close to either one or two, depending on the parameter values, the system size, and the entropy threshold, and no well-defined prethermal plateaus are observed. Our analysis distinguishes the melting of integrable dynamics from the subsequent decay of a prethermal plateau, which is observed in the SRN regime.
